use_case_name: Monitor Current and Past Auction Status

claims.content: The Customer wants to monitor current and past auctions by viewing the history of a specific product item. This includes auction status (Unscheduled, Scheduled, Current/Live, Closed), dates/times, bid counts, winning bidder information, and details on bids such as the customer's last bid, SmartBid (max bid), and the winning bid.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Customer wants to monitor current and past auctions by viewing the history of a specific product item. This includes auction status (Unscheduled, Scheduled, Current/Live, Closed), dates/times, bid counts, winning bidder information, and details on bids such as the customer's last bid, SmartBid (max bid), and the winning bid.

claims.content: Customer
The user is logged in as Auctioneer within the Auction Admin workspace.
The use case is triggered when the user selects the SKU History Page from the Auction Admin Main Menu, then enters the Product ID and clicks "Go."
The user selects the SKU History Page from the Auction Admin Main Menu.
The user enters the Product ID and clicks “Go.”
The system displays the search results in two sections: a top section with product summary data and a bottom section listing auction history data on separate lines.
The bottom section lists each auction record with Auction Status, Auction Sequence, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve Amount, High Bid, Number of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of selecting the SKU History Page from the Auction Admin Main Menu, the user selects the Customer History Page from the Auction Admin Main Menu to monitor a specific customer's auction status history.

Diverges from Step 2: Instead of entering a Product ID and clicking 'Go', the customer clicks the 'Recently Ended Auctions' link on the page, and the system displays the last 24 hours of auction history.
Diverges from Step 3: In the displayed search results, the user rearranges the default order of item attribute columns.

Diverges from Step 4: From the search results display, the user clicks the 'Export to Excel' button under the search results, and the system generates a CSV file of all data in the search results for manual tracking.

Diverges from Step 4: For won items, when the customer's default payment type is PayPal or Amazon Payments and they have not yet paid, the Payment Status column shows 'Not Paid' in bold red text and includes a link to the 'Returning Winner's Payments' page.

Diverges from Step 4: In the Bid History section, a current/live auction is shown as 'Active' in place of a closing date/time, while past auctions show the closing date/time, auction sequence numbers, product ID (SKU), the customer's last bid, SmartBid if placed, and the winning bid.

If the customer's search for the Product ID (SKU) in Step 2 returns no matches, the system displays a 'No Results' page that includes a 'Search Tips' section advising the user to check for typos/misspellings, remove unnecessary words like 'and', 'the', or 'a', try plural and singular forms, use fewer or more generic keywords, and contact support if the tips fail.

missing_aspects: EF-address-validation: The 'Confirm City, State, Zip with the customer' validation exception (EC-EF-008) cannot be anchored because main_flow Step 2 is a Product ID search; main_flow should be extended with a Customer History/customer-search step.

EF-deactivated-account: The deactivated-account red-text display (EC-EF-006) applies to customer search results and cannot be anchored to the current SKU-history main_flow; a customer-search step is needed.

EF-not-paid: The unpaid PayPal/Amazon Payments 'Not Paid' status and Returning Winner's Payments hyperlink (EC-EF-001, EC-EF-002) require an order-status/customer-history step in main_flow to anchor; the exit/handoff to payment is not specified.
EF-cancelled-order: The cancelled-order red-text display (EC-EF-007) requires an Order History section step in main_flow to anchor; no recovery/exit beyond the visual flag is documented.
EF-no-results-recovery: After the No Results page, no explicit retry/return-to-Step-2 behavior is documented; only Search Tips and support contact are specified.
Explicit confirmation of whether the exception flow terminates or allows further interaction after displaying the No Results page.

claims.content: For the specified SKU, the system displays the SKU auction performance history in two sections: a top section with product summary data (Product ID, description, type, cost, price, thumbnail image, auction history metrics, buyer name, inventory quantities, and active date) and a bottom section listing individual auction records on separate lines with Auction Status, Auction Sequence, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve Amount (Opening Bid), High Bid, Number of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder.

The system displays the current and past auction status details to the customer, including the Product Description/Specifications section (with SKU, Type, Brand, Width, Metal Type, etc.) and the Item Bid History section (listing Name, Amount, Date Placed, and SmartBid User? for each bid).

The system displays the customer's current and past auction status history, including a Bid History section that lists each auction record with closing date/time (or 'Active' for live auctions), auction sequence numbers, product ID (SKU) numbers, the customer's last bid, SmartBid if placed, and the winning bid. Cancelled orders appear in RED.

On the customer's My Bid History page, the system displays items the customer previously bid on (won and not won), sorted by ending time with the most recent on top, with linked Item #s to Product Details; for won items, a Payment Status column shows 'Paid' or 'Not Paid', and if unpaid via PayPal/Amazon, 'Not Paid' appears in bold red and links to the Returning Winner's Payments page.

missing_aspects: PO-auction-status-category-enumeration: No valid postcondition evidence card explicitly enumerates the four auction status categories (Unscheduled, Scheduled, Current/Live, Closed) from the scope contract.

quality_flags.detail: [goal_mainflow_alignment] The goal is over-broad and inconsistent with main_flow. Main_flow implements a Customer-facing SKU History flow (select SKU History page, enter Product ID, view auction history), but the goal names Internal users and adds Customer History, order statuses, and payment/order-status details that are not present in main_flow. These extra elements belong to separate use cases and also leave downstream exception aspects unanchored. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Evidence for monitoring 'specific product item (SKU History)' is located on Page 96 (EC-G-001), but the claim cites EC-G-000 which only covers general auction monitoring.; Evidence for specific details like 'bid counts' and 'winning bidder information' is found in the SKU History mockup (Page 96) or Customer History requirements (Page 109), but these pages are not cited in the claim's evidence_refs.))

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] The Main Flow is a SKU History search: it selects the SKU History Page, enters a Product ID, and displays SKU auction records. Postconditions 2, 3, and 4 promise different views that this flow never opens: a Product Description/Specifications + Item Bid History view, a customer's Bid History with last bid/SmartBid/cancelled orders, and the customer's My Bid History page with payment status. Those postconditions are therefore unreachable from the described Main Flow. (still no supporting evidence after retrieval)

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] The main flow is an Auction Admin SKU History lookup: select the page, enter a Product ID, click Go, and view two-section SKU results. Postcondition 1 is reachable from that flow, but postconditions 2-4 describe customer-facing views (Product Description/Item Bid History, customer Bid History with SmartBid/cancelled-order formatting, and the customer's My Bid History page with Payment Status) that the main flow never opens or navigates to. These postconditions are therefore not reachable, breaking vertical flow continuity. (remove: target_claim_index -1 out of range)

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] The trigger/main flow are an Auction Admin SKU History lookup: select SKU History Page, enter Product ID, click Go, and view the resulting product summary and auction-record sections. The postconditions, however, include customer-facing outcomes that this main flow does not reach: Product Description/Item Bid History details, the customer's current-and-past auction status history with SmartBid/cancelled-order display, and the customer's My Bid History page with Payment Status and links to the Returning Winner's Payments page. No main-flow step navigates to these pages or sections, so the postcondition slot is not vertically continuous with the upstream flow.

[goal_mainflow_alignment] Main Flow Step 4 enumerates the displayed auction-history fields but omits the goal-required 'customer's last bid' and 'SmartBid (max bid)' details. The Goal explicitly includes these bid details, so the main successful path does not fully achieve the stated goal.

[altflow_diverge_points] Alternative Flow claim 1 diverges from Main Flow Step 1 by replacing the SKU History Page with the Customer History Page, changing the searched object from a product item to a customer. This is not a variant of the product-specific SKU-history main flow and does not fulfill the goal of viewing a specific product item's history; it is a separate use case.

inconsistency_hints: The Trigger states the use case starts when the user enters the Product ID and clicks Go, but the Main Flow begins one step earlier by selecting the SKU History Page from the Auction Admin Main Menu. This means the Main Flow restarts from a navigation step that should either be part of the Trigger or occur before it; as written, step 1 is not a continuation of the Trigger.

Main Flow step 2 changes the actor to 'the customer', while the Preconditions establish the logged-in user as an Auctioneer in the Auction Admin workspace and the Trigger/Main Flow step 1 use 'the user'. This is an actor discontinuity: the same flow cannot move from an Auctioneer entry context to a Customer performing the SKU entry action.

The goal claim is too broad: it names internal users, Customer History, and order statuses, while main_flow is a single SKU/Product-ID auction-history lookup. This conflates at least two distinct use cases (SKU History and Customer History/order status), so main_flow cannot satisfy the goal without being split.
Main flow does not contain the primary actor 'Customer' by name, exact role phrase, or pronoun; steps 1 and 2 use only the generic noun 'user'.
